module.title: Google Cloud deployment and network boundaries
module.summary: Place the Databricks account and both compute planes against Cinderline's organization, folders and projects, trace one query with a named identity at every hop, and diagnose a denied and an unreachable request in order while unverified Google Cloud capabilities stay unknown.
objectives: Draw Cinderline's Google Cloud deployment with every resource and service account in the project or account that owns it, and name what differs from AWS and Azure.
Trace author, control, execution and storage paths for one query on classic and on serverless compute, with bucket bindings and private connectivity at each boundary.
Run ordered diagnoses for a denied and an unreachable request and assemble an evidence matrix whose unknown cells stay unknown until verified.

scenarios.title: Write Cinderline's Google Cloud deployment note for security review
scenarios.context: Fictional Cinderline Components runs classic workspace cinderline-gcp-prod in project cl-dbx-prod, with its customer-managed VPC cl-vpc-dbx in network project cl-net-host, and is adding serverless workspace cinderline-gcp-sls in the same region. Sources: bucket gs://cl-quality-raw in project cl-data-lake, supplier Ardent Castings' bucket gs://ardent-parts-feed in Ardent's own organization, and a Cloud SQL instance on a private address in cl-vpc-dbx. Security requires no public egress from compute, private user access and named evidence for every boundary. Region, tier, release status and feature entitlement are unconfirmed.
scenarios.task: Produce a one-page deployment note for the security specialist: where every resource sits in Cinderline's organization and the Databricks account, one query's request path per plane with the identity at each hop, the storage identity and bucket binding for each source, the private connectivity required and its DNS, the two diagnostic sequences the operations team will follow, the unknowns with their owners, and what must not be copied from the AWS or Azure notes.
requirements: Place every resource in the project or account that owns it, including each service account read from its email.
Give each source its identity chain: principal, catalog grants, credential service account and the bucket binding with its owner, including the supplier's.
Separate the denied-request sequence from the unreachable-request sequence, with evidence rows for each.
Mark serverless private connectivity, required firewall rules, the default VM service account, tier and region as unknown until verified; provision nothing and copy no AWS or Azure answer.
scenarios.model:
### Placement
Databricks account: workspace objects for cinderline-gcp-prod (classic) and cinderline-gcp-sls (serverless), the control plane and the Unity Catalog metastore. Cinderline's organization: folder manufacturing holds cl-dbx-prod (cluster VMs, two workspace buckets) and cl-data-lake (gs://cl-quality-raw); folder shared-network holds cl-net-host (cl-vpc-dbx, node subnet dbx-nodes-use4, endpoint subnet). Service accounts, read from their emails: dbx-provisioner@cl-admin-tools (Cinderline, account admin); db-<workspace-id>@prod-gcp-us-east4 (a Databricks project; its roles in cl-dbx-prod to be captured); cred_quality's Databricks-managed account.

### Request paths
Classic: Ana signs in → the job runs as sp-quality-nightly → Unity Catalog checks its grants → a VM in cl-dbx-prod reaches the relay through relay-pe → it reads gs://cl-quality-raw as cred_quality's account. Serverless: the same principal, grants and credential; no Cinderline VM, subnet or NAT.

### Storage identity
gs://cl-quality-raw: bindings for cred_quality's email, made by the data platform team. gs://ardent-parts-feed: the same binding, made by Ardent's administrator; pending.

### Private connectivity
Back-end PSC: relay-pe and workspace-pe registered and listed as dataplane_relay and rest_api; a private gcp.databricks.com zone visible to cl-vpc-dbx with workspace, dp- and tunnel records; no Cloud NAT, so a package mirror must exist first. Front-end PSC from the transit VPC under ENDPOINT-level private access settings.

### Diagnoses
Denied: read the named layer → principal → grants or credential binding → Policy Troubleshooter → smallest grant → rerun → evidence row. Unreachable: resolve from the subnet → zone visibility → endpoint status → egress rules by priority → retest → evidence row.

### Unknown until verified
Serverless private access to the Cloud SQL lookup (kept on a classic job meanwhile); the firewall rules Databricks requires; the default VM service account; the workspace account's roles; PSC service attachments for the region; tier requirements for PSC and keys; whether Ardent's organization admits the binding. Nothing in this note is copied from the AWS or Azure notes.
scenarios.reasoning: The note keeps Google's hierarchy and the Databricks account apart, reads every service account's owner from its email, gives each source a complete chain that ends with a named binding owner, separates the two failure shapes so a permission fix is never applied to a network fault, and turns every unsettled capability into an owned verification item instead of a promise.

rubric.weak: One Databricks box; projects, folders and accounts merged.
rubric.partial: Projects named, but service accounts' owners guessed or AWS terms used.
rubric.strong: Every resource and service account placed in its owning project or account, read from emails and documented fields.

rubric.weak: Says 'grant access to the bucket' without naming who or what.
rubric.partial: Names the credential but not who makes the binding, or where.
rubric.strong: Principal, grants, credential account and binding owner for each source, including Ardent's administrator.

rubric.weak: One troubleshooting list mixing IAM and network checks.
rubric.partial: Separate lists, but in no defensible order or without evidence rows.
rubric.strong: A refusal read from its named layer; a timeout walked from name to endpoint to rule, each with evidence rows.

rubric.weak: Serverless PSC claimed from an SDK field or an Azure note.
rubric.partial: Unknowns listed without sources, owners or a fallback.
rubric.strong: Each unknown names its source, owner and fallback; nothing provisioned or borrowed from another cloud.

disclosures.question: Will Ardent bind our credential's service account on their bucket?
disclosures.response: Unknown. Ardent's security contact has not answered, and their organization may restrict which outside identities can be granted roles. Until they answer, the supplier source is marked unreadable in the design.

disclosures.question: Can serverless compute reach the Cloud SQL instance privately?
disclosures.response: The account team has not confirmed Google Cloud availability, region or release status in writing. The lookup stays on a classic job until they do.

disclosures.question: May the network team remove Cloud NAT when back-end PSC goes live?
disclosures.response: For control-plane traffic, yes. But three notebooks install packages from the public index today, so the platform team must provide a mirror before the NAT goes.

claims.description: In Google Cloud's resource hierarchy the organization is the root node, folders organize an organization's resources and a project's parent is an organization or a folder; the IAM policies evaluated for a permission can include policies inherited from the organization, folder and project; organization policy constraints restrict resource configuration and are inherited down the hierarchy, where they can be overridden.
claims.context: Google Cloud resource hierarchy and policy inheritance, from Google's published API descriptions.

claims.description: A classic Databricks workspace on Google Cloud names, as its cloud resource container, the project it uses to instantiate the workspace's cloud resources, plus a region; its network configuration records the project that holds the VPC and subnet; by default Databricks creates a VPC in that project for each workspace, a customer-managed VPC is recommended and an existing workspace cannot be migrated to one; account-level APIs are called by account admins with Google-issued OIDC tokens at accounts.gcp.databricks.com.
claims.context: Databricks on Google Cloud classic workspaces; region, tier and entitlement must be verified.

claims.description: A serverless workspace on Google Cloud is created with compute mode SERVERLESS and a region and needs no prerequisite resources; Databricks' reference template gives it no project container and no network configuration; the account API's storage modes are CUSTOMER_HOSTED and DEFAULT_STORAGE; classic workspaces report the effective compute mode HYBRID.
claims.context: Databricks on Google Cloud serverless workspaces; availability by region and account must be verified.

claims.description: A Google service account is owned by the project named when it is created, which forms part of its email; the workspace service account has the form db-<workspace-id>@prod-gcp-<region>.iam.gserviceaccount.com; provisioning uses a customer service account added to the Databricks account console as an account admin and granted a custom Workspace Creator role; a cluster can carry a Google service account used for Cloud Storage and BigQuery; the service account with access to a customer-managed key exists within the Databricks control-plane project; a Compute Engine VM supports one attached service account whose tokens code on the VM reads through the metadata server.
claims.context: Identities in a Databricks on Google Cloud deployment; the default classic VM account is not settled by these sources.

claims.description: On Google Cloud a Unity Catalog storage credential creates a Databricks-managed service account whose email is granted access to buckets, and Databricks' Unity Catalog guide binds roles/storage.objectAdmin and roles/storage.legacyBucketReader on the bucket; an external location combines a gs:// path with a storage credential; with uniform bucket-level access only bucket-level or higher IAM policies control access; testIamPermissions reports the permissions the caller itself holds on a bucket.
claims.context: Unity Catalog storage access on Google Cloud; minimum roles must be read from the current Databricks page.

claims.description: A customer-managed VPC for a classic workspace on Google Cloud supplies a subnet in the workspace's region, with a netmask between /29 and /9, from whose range Compute Engine cluster nodes are allocated, and outbound access to the public network through Cloud NAT or a similar customer-managed appliance; one VPC can serve several workspaces but a subnet cannot be reused by other workspaces or resources; secondary pod and service ranges and the GKE configuration are deprecated and no longer supported.
claims.context: Classic compute networking on Google Cloud; firewall and Private Google Access requirements are not settled by these sources.

claims.description: Private Google Access lets VMs in a subnet reach Google services without external IP addresses; a Cloud NAT gateway lets VMs in the chosen subnets reach the internet without external IP addresses; a VM without an access configuration has no external internet access; Databricks' examples enable Private Google Access on the node subnet, and Databricks' reference template creates no Cloud Router or Cloud NAT when back-end Private Service Connect is used.
claims.context: Outbound paths from classic compute on Google Cloud.

claims.description: Google Cloud firewall rules allow or deny ingress or egress for instances in a VPC network; direction defaults to ingress; priority runs from 0 to 65535 with 1000 as default, lower numbers take precedence and a deny beats an allow at equal priority; implied rules sit at priority 65535; target tags or target service accounts narrow a rule, and without them it applies to every instance in the network; the Databricks Workspace Creator role includes permission to read and create firewall rules, and Databricks' reference template creates an ingress rule for the Databricks subnet before the workspace and, when hardened without PSC, an egress rule using the region's control-plane IP addresses.
claims.context: VPC firewall rules; the rules Databricks requires must be read from the current customer-managed VPC page.

claims.description: Back-end Private Service Connect for Databricks on Google Cloud uses two endpoints, one for the secure cluster connectivity relay and one for REST APIs; each is a forwarding rule in the customer's VPC whose target is a Databricks service attachment, registered in the Databricks account with its project, endpoint name and region and listed in the network configuration as dataplane_relay or rest_api; a workspace must be created with private access settings to support PSC scenarios; Databricks' reference template requires a customer-managed VPC and adds a private Cloud DNS zone for gcp.databricks.com, visible to the VPC, with records for the workspace URL, its dp- variant and tunnel.<region>.gcp.databricks.com; a PSC connection's status can be ACCEPTED, PENDING, REJECTED, CLOSED or NEEDS_ATTENTION.
claims.context: Classic private connectivity on Google Cloud; regional service attachments, tier and release status must be verified.

claims.description: A front-end PSC endpoint, placed in a transit VPC, carries user connections to the Databricks web application, REST API and Databricks Connect API; private access settings choose ACCOUNT level, which admits VPC endpoints registered in the Databricks account, or ENDPOINT level, which admits only listed endpoint IDs; public_access_enabled defaults to true on Google Cloud and false on AWS, and with public access enabled an IP access list restricts public sources; the API description allows disabling public access only with both front-end and back-end private connections.
claims.context: Front-end private connectivity and private access settings; the API description is partly worded for AWS.

claims.description: The Databricks Terraform provider documentation at v1.133.0 states that NCC binding is available for AWS and Azure only and in Public Preview on AWS, that NCC private endpoint rules are available on Azure and in Public Preview on AWS, and documents only AWS and Azure default and target rule types; the Databricks SDK for Python v0.141.0 models a gcp_endpoint on NCC private endpoint rules with a target service attachment, Google API hostnames or all APIs that support VPC Service Controls; network policies list GOOGLE_CLOUD_STORAGE as a storage destination type.
claims.context: Serverless connectivity on Google Cloud: the read sources conflict, so availability is unknown until verified.

claims.description: On AWS the Databricks network configuration takes at least two subnets in different availability zones with netmasks between /17 and /25 plus security groups, and a storage credential's IAM role requires a trust policy; Azure Databricks workspaces are Azure resources whose injected virtual network uses two subnets delegated to Microsoft.Databricks/workspaces with network security groups, with Private Link private endpoints for back-end, front-end and browser authentication, and storage credentials can use an Azure Databricks access connector's managed identity.
claims.context: Contrast only; the AWS and Azure modules own their clouds' answers.

concepts.definition: The organization, folders and projects that contain Google Cloud resources and pass IAM and organization policies downward.
Compute Engine VMs in the customer's project for classic workspaces; Databricks-managed compute for serverless.
A Google Cloud identity for software, owned by the project whose ID appears in its email.
A Unity Catalog object backed by a Databricks-managed service account that must be granted roles on each bucket it reads.
A customer VPC registered with its project, VPC and one regional subnet, with an outbound path for classic nodes.
A network-wide allow or deny rule for ingress or egress, where the lowest priority number decides and a deny wins a tie.

concepts.term: Private Service Connect (Databricks on Google Cloud)
concepts.definition: Forwarding rules in the customer's VPC that target Databricks service attachments, registered in the account and resolved through private DNS.
The account object that governs serverless connections to customer resources on AWS and Azure; its Google Cloud availability is unknown until verified.
A status kept on a design cell until a named source or test settles the capability for the account, region and release.
Checks ordered by failure shape: follow the layer a refusal names, or walk the network path outward for a timeout.
